summary: Iteration 38 (Stripe Recurring Subscriptions + Premium gating) backend-only review. Wrote pytest suite covering 31 test cases across /api/subscriptions/* payload + Stripe gating, /api/auth/me premium flag, library/challenges/group-DM 200-vs-402 gating, and 8 regression endpoints. 30/31 pass. Single failure: POST /api/subscriptions/create-checkout-session returns 503 for the admin user instead of the expected 200 + already_premium=true — root cause is the `if not stripe_ready` 503 raise being placed BEFORE the `if is_premium_user(user)` short-circuit in subscriptions.py:181-195. All other contracts hold: admin status payload is_premium=true / is_admin_premium=true, non-admin is_premium=false, pricing.monthly=499c / pricing.annual=3999c, trial_days=7, stripe_ready=false; customer-portal & webhook both 503 with placeholder key; library/challenge/group-DM 402 detail contains the exact phrase 'Sanctus Premium is required'; all 5 papal encyclicals (humanae-vitae, veritatis-splendor, centesimus-annus, evangelii-nuntiandi, magnifica-humanitas) free for non-admin; confessions-augustine paywalled 402 for non-admin, 200 for admin; books list now carries `is_premium` bool (papal=false, others=true); challenges enroll 402/200; group DM 402/200; film ccc-bernadette-anim youtube_id still 'ACBWU4ug-rc'. Note: /api/saints/today and /api/daily-practice require a `?date=` query param (pre-existing, not a regression) — adjusted regression test accordingly.

critical.issue: Admin (philipwils13@gmail.com / user_ade7a898e281) receives 503 'Payments are not configured…' instead of the spec-required 200 + {already_premium: true, url: null}. Root cause: in /app/backend/subscriptions.py the `if not stripe_ready: raise 503` block runs BEFORE the `if is_premium_user(user): return {already_premium: True}` short-circuit. Fix: move the `is_premium_user(user)` check above the stripe_ready guard (or check it inside the 503 branch first). One-line ordering swap — purely business-logic, no Stripe call needed for premium accounts.

action_items: Swap the ordering in /app/backend/subscriptions.py inside create_checkout(): check `if is_premium_user(user): return {already_premium: True, url: None}` BEFORE the `if not stripe_ready: raise 503`. This is required by the explicit spec: admin must receive 200/already_premium=true even when STRIPE_API_KEY is the placeholder.
critical_code_review_comments: subscriptions.py create_checkout: stripe_ready gate fires before the admin/already-premium short-circuit (lines 181-195). Spec says admin must short-circuit first; this is the sole failing test.

subscriptions.py:298 reads `subscription.current_period_end` directly. As of Stripe API 2025-09-30, `current_period_end` was relocated from the Subscription object to the line items. If the deployed Stripe account uses an API version after that change, this field will arrive None and premium.current_period_end will silently become null. Consider falling back to `items.data[0].current_period_end` (no fix required now since reconcile/webhook paths are 503-gated in preview).
subscriptions.py file is 521 lines — still within budget but approaching the 700-line ceiling; consider extracting the webhook handler into its own module before it grows further.

rca_of_issue: Bug: POST /api/subscriptions/create-checkout-session returns 503 for admin instead of 200/already_premium=true. Reproduce: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8001/api/subscriptions/create-checkout-session -H 'Authorization: Bearer test_premium_2453a541f1e0982d' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"plan":"monthly","return_origin":"http://localhost"}'` → 503. Root cause: subscriptions.py lines 181-195, the `if not stripe_ready` raise precedes the `if is_premium_user(user)` short-circuit, so admin accounts can never reach the already_premium branch in the placeholder-key preview environment. Mitigation: swap the two if-blocks so the admin check runs first.
